title: Rooming houses and drinking-musician reputation in Fort Worth
summary: Hotels were scarce; landlords disliked musicians' late hours.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you have any kinds of experiences in Texas or Kansas City or other parts of maybe Louisiana or other parts of the South that weren't pleasant?

Well, we had a little difficulty in Fort Worth, Texas. We had to find a...we called them a rooming house; a boarding house, rather. There wasn't much hotels, so when we get to a new place, we'd get some kind of place that... Two of the boys would stay at this house here, and... Sometimes them people down South, they owned two or three homes down there, you know. And they wasn't tickled about takin' in musicians, because they'd heard about musicians. The musician had a bad name. I know why. They come in late hours. The musicians do a lot of drinking, stay up all night long and blow their horn, you know, in your house. People didn't like that so well.
Well, we made out all right, but...
